newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean stocks close lower as blue chips fall.
newsitem.headline: South Korean stocks close lower as blue chips fall.

text.p: Profit-taking in blue chips and foreign selling of bank shares sent Seoul stock index to a lower close on Thursday, brokers said.
A news report that the brokerages' group called for steps to boost the stock market had no immediate impact. Brokers said investors doubted if the government would accept the request.
The index closed 4.97 points, or 0.76 percent, lower at 651.65. It fluctuated between 651.59 to 665.57.
Ssangyong Motor went daily limit-up on renewed rumours -- denied by the two companies -- that it was a target of Samsung Group's takeover bid.

Ssangyong closed 450 won higher at 6,170. But investors shrugged off a report a Ssangyong Group executive forecast the auto maker's loss would cut to 150 billion won this year from 228.5 billion last year.
"It made no impact as investors thought the forecast was too optimistic," said a broker at Daishin Securities.
Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities said blue chips lost ground. "Many investors chased for quick profits as they are lack of confidence about the market's outlook," Koh said.
Samsung Electronics fell 2,000 won to 58,000 and Korea Electric Power was down 300 won to 26,000.

Chairman Youn Young-kyu of the Korea Securities Dealers' Association called for steps to boost the stock market, including the expansion of the foreign share ownership ceiling to 30 percent this year from the current 20 percent.
Youn made the requests when he met ruling New Korea Party's chairman Lee Hoi-chang.
Hit by foreign selling, Cho Hung Bank closed 120 won lower at 4,350 and Korea First Bank fell 50 won to end at 3,350.
